answer: A verifiable delay function bound to each identity key acts as a ferrous anchor: before an agent earns full harbor rights in the shared market, it must finish a sequential computation that cannot be parallelized or outsourced, taking minutes of real CPU time per identity. A sybil operator spawning a nebula of thousands of fake agents must pay that compute cost for every single clone, while honest agents pay it once, so mass fakery becomes economically ruinous and each identity cost stays verifiable on-chain.
